patterns.title: Eyebrows above every heading
patterns.signal: Repeated small labels restate headings without adding navigation or meaning.
patterns.reason: A default section template replaces information hierarchy.
patterns.fix: Remove redundant labels; let headings and spacing establish hierarchy.
patterns.exception: A real category, breadcrumb, or required editorial label can orient the reader.
patterns.example: FEATURES above Our features above a feature list.
patterns.counterexample: A research article labels its section Methods to distinguish it from Results.

patterns.title: Badges everywhere
patterns.signal: Pills, chips, and status dots decorate most headings or cards without distinct semantics.
patterns.reason: Decoration competes with the information and real states.
patterns.fix: Reserve badges for useful status, taxonomy, counts, or filtering.
patterns.exception: A dense operations table can legitimately show many independent live states.
patterns.example: Every feature has NEW, PRO, or AI POWERED with no behavioral meaning.
patterns.counterexample: A deployment dashboard marks failed and pending jobs with accessible status labels.

patterns.title: Comments narrating obvious code
patterns.signal: Comments repeat the next expression, type, or function name.
patterns.reason: Comment volume substitutes for clear names and reasoning.
patterns.fix: Delete narration; retain rationale, invariants, hazards, public contracts, and legal notices.
patterns.exception: Explain a nonobvious constraint even when the code itself is short.
patterns.example: # Increment count immediately before count += 1.
patterns.counterexample: A comment explains why a retry must not repeat a non-idempotent payment.

patterns.title: Tests with no meaningful oracle
patterns.signal: Assertions are tautologies, compare a value to itself, or check only that a mock returns its configured value.
patterns.reason: A green suite is confused with evidence of required behavior.
patterns.fix: Assert an independently specified observable outcome at a public seam; prove a relevant wrong implementation fails.
patterns.exception: A small invariant or reviewed snapshot can be valuable when it catches a meaningful regression.
patterns.example: assert result == result or assert True after calling an empty stub.
patterns.counterexample: A provider contract rejects a response missing a consumer-required field.

patterns.title: Template-driven card grids
patterns.signal: Unrelated content is forced into identical cards, nested cards, or repeated three-column sections.
patterns.reason: A convenient component substitutes for the content structure.
patterns.fix: Use layout suited to comparison, sequence, reading, or action; flatten needless wrappers.
patterns.exception: A product catalog or comparable items can benefit from a consistent card grid.
patterns.example: A legal policy is split into pricing-style cards.
patterns.counterexample: Comparable projects each show a preview, title, owner, and useful action.

patterns.title: Unmotivated visual effects
patterns.signal: Glass, glow, gradients, giant blurred orbs, or faux grain repeat without supporting the brief.
patterns.reason: A fashionable effect is used as a substitute for visual direction.
patterns.fix: Choose effects from the subject, brand, materials, and hierarchy; remove unsupported flourishes.
patterns.exception: A requested neon poster, frosted material study, or established brand gradient is intentional.
patterns.example: An accounting form gets neon glows and a huge gradient orb behind every field.
patterns.counterexample: A concert poster uses glowing type consistent with its night-club brief.

patterns.title: Ornamental typography without hierarchy
patterns.signal: Tracked uppercase labels, arbitrary italic words, or highlighted words appear as repeated decoration.
patterns.reason: A typography trick takes the place of a readable hierarchy.
patterns.fix: Use coherent type roles and emphasize only semantic distinctions.
patterns.exception: An editorial identity or a diagram can intentionally need these treatments.
patterns.example: Every headline colors one arbitrary word despite identical meaning.
patterns.counterexample: A language lesson highlights the particular word whose pronunciation is being taught.

patterns.title: Invented credibility
patterns.signal: Metrics, logos, citations, testimonials, case studies, or provenance claims lack a verified source.
patterns.reason: Plausible detail is mistaken for factual evidence.
patterns.fix: Remove unsupported claims or clearly label approved fictional/mock content; preserve real evidence.
patterns.exception: Explicitly fictional art and clearly labeled sample data do not claim to be real.
patterns.example: A live product page claims 10,000 customers and shows companies never consulted.
patterns.counterexample: A prototype visibly labels its sample customer quote as placeholder content.

patterns.title: Decorative or simulated functionality
patterns.signal: Controls do nothing, links point nowhere, or success states appear without the operation succeeding.
patterns.reason: A screenshot is optimized while the actual task remains impossible.
patterns.fix: Wire the requested behavior, expose honest unavailable states, and validate real boundaries.
patterns.exception: A visibly labeled static mockup may intentionally demonstrate only appearance.
patterns.example: A signup form always displays Success without sending or storing anything.
patterns.counterexample: A disabled preview button explains that this prototype does not submit data.

patterns.title: Only the happy-path screenshot works
patterns.signal: Loading, empty, error, long-content, keyboard, or narrow-screen states break required use.
patterns.reason: A single attractive frame is treated as the complete experience.
patterns.fix: Inspect relevant states at realistic content and viewport sizes; repair task and accessibility failures.
patterns.exception: Do not invent product states outside the task; assess those the real flow requires.
patterns.example: A fixed-width checkout hides its submit button on a phone.
patterns.counterexample: A responsive table has a usable small-screen reading path and visible keyboard focus.

patterns.title: Data-like decoration
patterns.signal: Charts, terminal text, status lights, or technical-looking labels imply data that does not exist.
patterns.reason: The appearance of technical substance stands in for meaning.
patterns.fix: Use actual explained data or remove the pseudo-information.
patterns.exception: An openly fictional sci-fi interface can use decorative telemetry.
patterns.example: A sales dashboard draws unlabeled random bars as evidence of growth.
patterns.counterexample: A chart names its measure, interval, source, and actual values.

patterns.title: Abstractions without a present need
patterns.signal: Factories, wrappers, plugin layers, or config machinery have no current caller or requirement.
patterns.reason: Imagined flexibility inflates the maintenance surface.
patterns.fix: Implement the smallest coherent current behavior and keep justified extension seams.
patterns.exception: A demonstrated second implementation, public interface, or actual variation can justify abstraction.
patterns.example: A one-use formatter gets an abstract factory and registry of providers.
patterns.counterexample: Two supported backends share a small tested storage contract.

patterns.title: Defensive noise and hidden failures
patterns.signal: Broad catches, impossible guards, or fallback values hide broken invariants or failures.
patterns.reason: Appearing robust masks uncertainty about the contract.
patterns.fix: Validate real trust boundaries; propagate or handle failures explicitly at the correct owner.
patterns.exception: Untrusted input and genuinely recoverable failures require validation and narrow recovery.
patterns.example: catch Exception returns an empty list after a required database write fails.
patterns.counterexample: An HTTP boundary validates external JSON and returns a specific input error.

patterns.title: Type escapes replacing a contract
patterns.signal: Any casts, ignored diagnostics, or unchecked coercions suppress a real interface mismatch.
patterns.reason: Removing a compiler complaint is mistaken for fixing behavior.
patterns.fix: Model the boundary and narrow unknown input with actual validation.
patterns.exception: A documented, narrow interop shim may be necessary for an untyped library.
patterns.example: Cast a failed payment response to any so the success renderer compiles.
patterns.counterexample: A validated discriminated union distinguishes success from failure.

patterns.title: Boilerplate and dependency bloat
patterns.signal: Unrequested scaffolding, dependencies, duplicated helpers, or generated layers dominate a small change.
patterns.reason: Output volume substitutes for a complete minimal deliverable.
patterns.fix: Reuse the local idioms and remove unused machinery while preserving required behavior.
patterns.exception: Generated protocol bindings and required framework glue can be large and justified.
patterns.example: A two-line parsing fix introduces a new framework and parallel utility hierarchy.
patterns.counterexample: A required client binding is generated from the pinned service contract.

patterns.title: Placeholder work reported as complete
patterns.signal: TODO stubs, canned return values, omitted branches, or unrun checks are described as finished or verified.
patterns.reason: A completion narrative replaces delivery evidence.
patterns.fix: Implement the authorized behavior or state the exact remaining limitation and verification status.
patterns.exception: A requested scaffold may contain clearly labeled placeholders.
patterns.example: A function returns a hardcoded success while the report says production-ready and tested.
patterns.counterexample: A scaffold report identifies its stub and states which checks actually ran.

patterns.title: Tests mirror the implementation
patterns.signal: Expected values are recomputed with the same algorithm or copied from unreviewed output.
patterns.reason: The oracle repeats the same mistake as the code.
patterns.fix: Derive expectations from examples, invariants, requirements, or a real independent contract.
patterns.exception: A separately derived reference implementation can serve as an independent oracle.
patterns.example: The test imports the function to calculate its own expected result.
patterns.counterexample: A tax example uses an independently calculated amount from the published rule.

patterns.title: Mocks posing as contracts
patterns.signal: Tests prove internal calls or mutually agreeing mocks without exercising the consumer/provider boundary.
patterns.reason: An implementation detail is confused with externally required behavior.
patterns.fix: Verify actual boundary serialization, validation, and compatibility against the real provider implementation or its verified contract.
patterns.exception: A narrowly isolated unit test may use mocks; call counts matter for explicit side-effect or resource limits.
patterns.example: Both sides mock the same assumed response and declare API compatibility.
patterns.counterexample: A consumer-required schema is checked against actual provider responses in isolation.

patterns.title: Redundant tests for appearance
patterns.signal: Many tests restate the same outcome or assert implementation details without covering distinct risks.
patterns.reason: Test count and line coverage replace behavioral confidence.
patterns.fix: Keep distinct behavior and boundary cases; remove duplicates and brittle private-detail assertions.
patterns.exception: A data-driven matrix is justified when cases exercise materially different boundaries.
patterns.example: Twenty tests each assert that a trivial getter returns the fixture value.
patterns.counterexample: Boundary cases cover zero, maximum, missing, and invalid quantities with specified outcomes.

patterns.title: Green by weakening the test
patterns.signal: Assertions are deleted, expectations copy a bug, or tests are skipped solely to remove a failure.
patterns.reason: A green indicator becomes the goal instead of the required outcome.
patterns.fix: Determine whether the implementation or requirement changed; retain a test that distinguishes the intended behavior.
patterns.exception: A documented obsolete requirement can justify revising or retiring its test.
patterns.example: Skip the regression test after the fix fails, then report all checks green.
patterns.counterexample: Update a contract only after an explicit requirement change and show its new behavioral evidence.

patterns.title: Inflation without a concrete claim
patterns.signal: Grand significance, generic praise, vague authority, or corporate verbs replace a specific actor and action.
patterns.reason: The language sounds substantial without communicating evidence.
patterns.fix: State the supported fact, action, example, or uncertainty in the intended voice.
patterns.exception: Expressive or promotional writing can be appropriate when its claims remain grounded.
patterns.example: This groundbreaking solution revolutionizes seamless collaboration without saying what it does.
patterns.counterexample: The tool assigns each review comment to its owner and records its resolution.

patterns.title: Formulaic rhetorical scaffolding
patterns.signal: Repeated staged contrasts, forced triads, canned summaries, or synonym cycling organize otherwise simple points.
patterns.reason: A familiar rhetorical template overwhelms the actual argument.
patterns.fix: Keep the logical relation and natural rhythm; cut scaffolding that adds no meaning.
patterns.exception: A real contrast, three genuine alternatives, or requested formal summary can help comprehension.
patterns.example: Every paragraph ends with an inspirational takeaway and repeats the same contrast.
patterns.counterexample: A technical comparison explicitly contrasts latency and throughput because the decision depends on them.

patterns.title: Formatting as substance
patterns.signal: Fragments, excessive bold labels, unnecessary tables, or repetitive headings inflate a small answer.
patterns.reason: Visual structure is mistaken for explanatory content.
patterns.fix: Use connected prose or a compact structure appropriate to the actual information.
patterns.exception: A real mapping, sequence, or long reference benefits from a table or headings.
patterns.example: A one-step answer has six headings, bold labels, and a recap.
patterns.counterexample: A compatibility matrix presents actual differences across five platforms.

patterns.title: Invented personal voice
patterns.signal: Fake anecdotes, deliberate errors, or invented sensory experience are added to appear human.
patterns.reason: Humanization is confused with fabricated evidence or caricature.
patterns.fix: Preserve the actual author voice and supported experience; improve specificity without invention.
patterns.exception: Clearly fictional narration may use an invented first-person speaker.
patterns.example: An editor invents a childhood memory for the author of a factual article.
patterns.counterexample: An edit keeps the supplied real anecdote and removes generic connective filler.

patterns.title: Verification and certainty overclaims
patterns.signal: A report claims tests, renders, media inspection, deployment, or certainty beyond what was observed.
patterns.reason: Confidence and clean phrasing hide the evidence boundary.
patterns.fix: Separate edited, run, observed, and unresolved; keep caveats that change the decision.
patterns.exception: A concise report can state verified outcomes when actual evidence supports them.
patterns.example: Say visually verified after reading only CSS, or tests passed without running them.
patterns.counterexample: State source checked; rendered layout not inspected when no renderer was available.

patterns.title: Generic output that misses the brief
patterns.signal: Polished stock tropes replace the specified subject, audience, materials, story, or product task.
patterns.reason: Surface polish is mistaken for requirement satisfaction.
patterns.fix: Compare the actual artifact with the brief; choose subject-specific composition and assets.
patterns.exception: A stock aesthetic can be correct when explicitly requested and relevant.
patterns.example: A requested repair tutorial becomes a cinematic montage with no visible repair steps.
patterns.counterexample: A repair sequence clearly shows each requested operation with consistent parts.

patterns.title: Unintentional geometry artifacts
patterns.signal: Anatomy, joints, objects, reflections, occlusion, shadows, or perspective are incoherent in inspected regions.
patterns.reason: Local plausibility fails to form a consistent physical scene.
patterns.fix: Inspect the full image and relevant closeups or frames; repair the actual inconsistent region.
patterns.exception: Surreal, diagrammatic, or intentionally impossible geometry may be the brief.
patterns.example: A hand grows a sixth finger while gripping a physically disconnected handle.
patterns.counterexample: An intentionally Escher-like illustration follows its requested impossible-space concept.

patterns.title: Garbled or meaningless visual text
patterns.signal: Requested text, signage, labels, or logos are unreadable, misspelled, duplicated, or semantically wrong.
patterns.reason: Text-like shapes stand in for required information.
patterns.fix: Use accurate typography or regenerate/edit the actual asset, then inspect at delivery size.
patterns.exception: Abstract texture can resemble text when no readable message is intended.
patterns.example: A product image misspells the required model name on its packaging.
patterns.counterexample: An abstract artwork uses letter-like marks without claiming they are readable copy.

patterns.title: Unrequested plastic or overprocessed materials
patterns.signal: Waxy skin, uniform gloss, oversharpened edges, fake bokeh, or incoherent detail erase required material qualities.
patterns.reason: A generic polished finish substitutes for appropriate texture and optics.
patterns.fix: Match the requested medium, lighting, materials, and level of finish.
patterns.exception: Glossy toys, beauty retouching, or stylized renders can intentionally use these qualities.
patterns.example: A documentary portrait has plastic skin and painted-on texture despite a natural-light brief.
patterns.counterexample: A shiny vinyl character render intentionally uses smooth reflective surfaces.

patterns.title: Identity or scene drift
patterns.signal: Required characters, products, materials, lighting, or art direction change inconsistently across regions or shots.
patterns.reason: Independent generations fail the continuity requirement.
patterns.fix: Track required identities and scene constraints; compare references and shots before delivery.
patterns.exception: A story can intentionally change time, lighting, costume, or visual style.
patterns.example: A product switches its control layout between demonstration shots with no explanation.
patterns.counterexample: A time-lapse intentionally changes lighting while preserving the product geometry.

patterns.title: Temporal artifacts and meaningless motion
patterns.signal: Objects morph, edges flicker, limbs appear, continuity breaks, or transitions obscure the requested action.
patterns.reason: A plausible frame is confused with a coherent sequence.
patterns.fix: Watch the relevant sequence in motion; inspect suspect frames and repair continuity or timing.
patterns.exception: Deliberate morph animation, jump cuts, and experimental flicker can be intentional.
patterns.example: A cup handle dissolves halfway through an otherwise realistic pour.
patterns.counterexample: An explicitly requested morph transition transforms one object into another.

patterns.title: Unintentional audio artifacts
patterns.signal: Clipping, repeated phrases, timing gaps, synthetic prosody, or identity drift conflict with required intelligibility and continuity.
patterns.reason: A generated track is delivered without listening to the actual sequence.
patterns.fix: Listen at the intended playback level and check relevant transitions, pronunciation, and sync.
patterns.exception: A robotic voice, distortion, or abrupt cut may be an explicit artistic choice.
patterns.example: A narration repeats a sentence and clips the start of the next required instruction.
patterns.counterexample: A requested radio-robot effect intentionally uses distortion while keeping instructions intelligible.
